editorial_angle: The article says the weather was rebuilt. The video asks the only question a player cares about: what happens to a police chase when the hurricane hits? It opens on the consequence, gives the two facts that are on record, names the thing Rockstar has not said, and then plays the chase through the storm as a clearly labelled what-if.

entertainment_angle.surprising_fact: Rockstar rebuilt the whole weather system and put hurricanes in the game, then said nothing about whether they affect how you play.
entertainment_angle.entertaining_consequence: If the storm is more than scenery, the police chase every player knows by heart falls apart: no grip, no visibility, no usual way out.
entertainment_angle.visual_opportunity: A red sports car hydroplaning through floodwater at night with police lights behind it.
entertainment_angle.relatable_scenario: You are at maximum wanted level, flooring it to the escape route you always use.
entertainment_angle.wait_what_moment: The road you are escaping on is under water, and the cops chasing you are spinning out too.
entertainment_angle.why_viewers_care: Everyone who has played an open-world game has run from the police. Nobody has done it in a hurricane.

editing_notes: Frame one is the slide: no fade-in, no title. The first caption is on screen with the first word. The narrator leads and the cuts follow his full stops. Shots 5 to 8 are the escalation and get faster: one consequence, one cut. Leave a beat of near silence before 'You're cooked'. The last shot is the opening slide slowed down: it lets the question land and loops cleanly into frame one. Tags stay small in the corner: ON RECORD for the two facts, NOT CONFIRMED for the question, WHAT IF for everything we are imagining. No HUD, no wanted stars on screen, nothing that imitates a game interface.
sound_music: Rain and wind from the first frame. Tyres, sirens and water for the slide; a thunderclap as the storm front appears; a riser into the cut to 'You're cooked' and a bass hit on it; screech and spin-out at the junction; a straining rotor for the helicopter; brakes and sloshing water at the dead end; then the music thins under the last question. The voice is always on top.
